description: Rendering foundation: PMREM environment lighting (RoomEnvironment for interior, PMREM-from-sky-scene for dusk), tuned ACES exposure per set, softer PCF shadows (PCFSoftShadowMap is removed in three 0.186), procedural DataTexture library from pure seeded generators, upgraded PBR material palette (all existing keys kept), a geometry kit with a mergeGeometries Batcher, full dispose(), and a renderInfo() test hook. Existing sets keep building unchanged on top of it. Detail: plan.md '3D realism upgrade' item 1 and 'Design decisions'.

findings: SIZES: build OK, dist\assets\scene-*.js 570.74 kB raw / 145.47 kB gzip (baseline 555/140, budget 680/175). TESTS: unit 6 files / 63 tests pass (23 old + texture-data 35 + geometry-kit 5). e2e 42/42 pass (5.1 min vs 1.7 min baseline; WebGL page reaches data-scene-ready in about 8-10 s under SwiftShader, was ~12 s before PMREM size was cut to 128, so keep extra start-up work small; 20 s limit). Screenshots were regenerated by the e2e run; ch1/ch3 at 1440 checked visually: textures + env light read, no errors. Old residence geometry still uses stretched unit-box UVs (giant planks) and the F1 cream lamp plane is still there: FEAT-003 rebuilds. renderInfo() is wired but not yet asserted by e2e (FEAT-004 adds that test). API FOR LATER FEATS: lighting = createLighting(scene, renderer) -> { hemi, sun, sky, envDusk, envInterior, setFocus, setTime, follow, setEnvironment(set), dispose }. envDusk/envInterior are THREE.Texture (PMREM, 128 px) or null without a renderer; index.js already sets mats.glass/lowIron/river.envMap = lighting.envDusk. For new outdoor materials created inside sets (tower glass, skyline facades, river) either reuse mats.glass/mats.river or pass lighting.envDusk into the set (createX(mats) has no env access today; e.g. give sets an extra arg or set it in index.js after build). Exposure: showSet sets renderer.toneMappingExposure 0.95 exterior / 1.0 residence; envIntensity 0.6 / 0.35; hemi 0.35 - 0.1k. scene object: info() -> {calls, triangles}; window.__tessera.renderInfo() -> scene ? scene.info() : null. dispose() traverses scene (geometries/materials/textures in Sets, skips isRenderTargetTexture, InstancedMesh.dispose), then mats.dispose(), clearGeometryCache(), lighting.dispose(), renderer.dispose(). TEXTURES (src/scene/textures.js): colorTexture(name) sRGB albedo, roughnessTexture(name) from alpha, dataTexture(name) raw linear (bump/normal/alpha), repeated(texture, x, y=x) cached clone sharing the Source (use this for per-surface repeat; base textures have repeat 1), disposeTextures(). Names: oak, walnut, marble, travertine, linen, boucle, concrete, brushedMetal, woolRug (clamp, single rug image), waterNormal, contactShadow (clamp). Roughness in alpha for oak, walnut, marble, travertine, concrete; linen/boucle/brushedMetal are grey luminance; waterNormal is a tangent normal map. OAK TILE = 8 planks x 180 mm = 1.44 m across u, 2.88 m along v (grain along v): repeat = (width/1.44, length/2.88). MATERIALS: all 17 old keys kept + walnut, marble, brass, bronze, linenOlive, linenPaper, boucle, leather, wool, ceramic, smokedGlass, leaf, soil, ledStrip, shadowDecal, plus dispose(). glass/lowIron/smokedGlass/ceramic are MeshPhysicalMaterial (glass: no transmission, opacity, depthWrite false, ior 1.5). Palette materials use base textures at repeat 1; set map/roughnessMap/bumpMap to repeated(...) variants on cloned materials or give geometry world-scaled UVs where tiling matters. GEOMETRY KIT (src/scene/geometry-kit.js): roundedBox(w,h,d,r,segments=3) cached+shared (do not mutate; indexed); lathe(points [[x,y]|Vector2], segs=48); tube(points [[x,y,z]|Vector3], radius, {tubularSegments=48, radialSegments=12, closed=false}); extrudeProfile(shape|[[x,y]], depth, bevel=0) centred on z, bevel grows the outline; cushion(w,h,d,sag,{radius=min*0.25, segments=16, round=3}) bottom flat at -h/2, top centre at h/2 - sag; contactShadow(w, d, mats) -> Mesh (shared unit plane, y 0.004, userData.decal = true); clearGeometryCache(). class Batcher: add(geometry, material, matrix?) clones+bakes the matrix, keeps position/normal/uv only, returns this; build({cast=true, receive=true}) -> THREE.Mesh[] (one per material) and resets. Mixed indexed/non-indexed parts of one material are all converted to non-indexed (ExtrudeGeometry is non-indexed, roundedBox/lathe/tube/Box are indexed). Mirroring matrices (negative scale) flip winding: avoid or use DoubleSide.
